2015_075_021015mtg.paragraph: Agenda and supporting materials for the Troy School District Board of Education workshop meeting of February 10, 2015, held at 6:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The packet covers a 2014 bond bid-package update, a food service equipment and temperature-monitoring update, 2014/2015 General Fund Budget Amendment #1, and a review of Chapter B board policies. The central item is Budget Amendment #1, which restates projected general fund revenue at $142,706,181 and expenditures at $143,627,633, driven largely by the closing of the Durant fund, which inflated both revenue and expenditure by $5,619,125, and by an increase in the MPSERS UAAL categorical rate.

FOOD SERVICE EQUIPMENT UPDATE. Troy began investigating a temperature monitoring system in November 2012 and installed a Smart Temps pilot unit at Larson in May 2014; as of February 2015 the system has been very dependable. It would monitor walk-ins, reach-ins and hot holding units and document food temperatures during preparation and serving, mandatory under HACCP and currently done manually. Listed Smart Temps clients include University of Michigan (most recent), Central Michigan, Ball State University, Notre Dame, Stanford, Saline Schools, Walled Lake Schools, West Bloomfield Schools, Jefferson County, Kentucky (largest district), and Michigan City Schools, Indiana; districts installed in 2008 were still operating strong in 2014, life expectancy could be 10 years or more, and technology changes about every 5 years. Annual monitoring provides unlimited Command Center logins, phone support, onsite training, loading of food and serving menus, automatic updates, monthly data logs, data archiving for 7 years, and alerts by SMS, e-mail and phone. Alternate vendor Great Lakes Hotel gave no response on monitoring costs; its reference School City of Hammond, Indiana (Dr. Julie Boettger) uses E-Control for walk-in coolers/freezers and dish machines only across 22 schools and is piloting Smart Temps, while Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools, North Carolina (Cindy Hobbs) and Charlotte County Public Schools (Don Buck) had not responded as of 2/4/15.

The 2013-2014 Food Service Fund equity schedule reports, for the June 2013 audit report, total program cost 3,152,489, three-month average operating cost 1,050,830, ending fund balance 1,098,915, and excess amount required to be drawn down $48,085; for the June 2014 unaudited report, 3,242,385, 1,079,714, 1,320,716 and $241,002, with $289,087 printed beneath. Total actual and anticipated expenditures $(463,829); anticipated balance of the Food Service Fund after equipment expenditures $856,887.

GENERAL FUND BUDGET AMENDMENT #1. A memorandum dated February 6, 2015 from Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services (4400 Livernois, phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013) to Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, describes the amendment presented at the February 10, 2015 workshop and recommended for approval March 3, 2015. Local revenue, from non-homestead and hold-harmless property tax valuations, gate receipts, interest and miscellaneous revenue collected by the City of Troy under a split levy of summer and winter collections, was not significantly impacted. State revenue is recommended to increase 7.6%, primarily from the State's payment to Local Education Agencies for the Michigan Public Schools Employee Retirement Systems Unfunded Actuarial Accrued Liability, with the rate increasing from 4.56% to 7.36%, approximately $3.3 million in additional revenue; January State Aid Status Report figures added $3.1 million. Federal revenue increased 2% for Adult Education, IDEA, IDEA Preschool, Title I, Title II and Title III. Incoming transfers and other transactions drove most of the 8.7% total revenue increase, chiefly closing the Durant fund as directed by auditors, inflating current year general fund revenues by $5,619,125; P.A. 18, the county-wide special education millage passed through Oakland Schools, was slightly decreased. Salaries were amended for an estimated $2.05 million increase from actual expenditures last year. Benefits rose 13% on the MPSERS UAAL accounting plus a 2.3% increase in the hard cap rate under P.A. 152. Contracted/purchased services cover PESG/ESR/ESS/Coach EZ Personnel, Enviro-Clean Services and First Student Transportation Services. Supplies and textbook lines decreased; capital outlay increased for Technology Readiness Infrastructure Grants (TRIG). Other expenses were reduced 104%, the original $1.5 million tax abatement/write-off assumption cut to $300,000 against expense to date of approximately $200,000 and a remainder not expected to exceed $100,000. Outgoing transfers and others increased 172% on the same $5,619,125. The memo concludes revenues increase approximately 9%, expenses approximately 8%, and the operating deficiency is reduced by 28% or $350,628 from the original adopted budget.

The Business Services Update presentation shows, across audited 6/30/2014, original budget 6/30/2015 and Amendment #1: projected revenue $132,580,491, $131,253,100, $142,706,181 (9%); projected expenditures $133,270,712, $132,525,180, $143,627,633 (8%); revenue under expenditures ($690,221), ($1,272,080), ($921,452) (-28%); beginning fund equity July 1 $22,070,236, $21,380,015, $21,380,015 (0%); ending fund equity June 30 $21,380,015, $20,107,935, $20,458,563 (2%); fund equity as a percent of expenditures 16%, 15%, 14%, and without the Durant transfer 16%, 15%, 15%. Revenue by source: 1XX Local $35,148,791, $36,487,546, $36,436,455 (-0.1%); 3XX State $87,238,767, $83,797,430, $90,201,335 (7.6%); 4XX Federal $2,900,197, $3,346,213, $3,414,552 (2.0%); 5XX Incoming Transfer & Other Transactions $7,292,736, $7,621,911, $12,653,839 (66.0%); total $132,580,491, $131,253,100, $142,706,181 (8.7%). State factors listed: 22a Prop A Obligation $2,491,157 with a $50 increase in the per pupil foundation allowance; 22b Discretionary Payment $631,434; 147C MPSERS UAAL Rate Stabilization Categorical (4.56% to 7.63%) $3,306,660; 22f Best Practice Incentive Categorical ($52 to $50) ($27,907). Out of district tuition decreased ($394,235) and Special Ed Public Act 18 revenue decreased ($192,962). The slide cites anticipated tax abatement write-offs of ($1.2 million) and the $5,619,125 Durant Fund close-out. The 2015-16 budget process calendar lists February for the Governor's Executive Budget, March-April for individual administration budget meetings, February-May to develop and confirm assumptions, March-June to develop the budget, a May/June public hearing and millage rate adoption, and June budget adoption; the general fund is amended three times per fiscal year (December, March, June) and special revenue funds twice (February and June).

POLICY REVIEW. The packet includes a page of the August 2013 Troy School District Board Policy table of contents (B-1206 Rules of Order through B-4001 Cable-casting of Board Meetings, plus Chapter C items C-1001 through C-1103) and full policy texts. B-1703 Suspension permits temporary suspension by a vote of four members (adopted April 8, 1975; revised January 16, 1979). B-1704 Notification requires first and second readings (adopted April 8, 1975; revised January 16, 1979 and July 10, 2007). B-1801 Policy Drafting reserves drafting to the Board and requires legal counsel review. B-1901 gives the superintendent power to act absent policy. B-2001 requires prior approval by resolution for out-of-state meetings (adopted June 21, 1976; revised March 17, 1998). B-2002 sets board member compensation at $100 per annum (adopted January 16, 1979; revised March 17, 1998 and April 15, 2003). B-2101 bars member conflicts of interest and hiring of immediate family during a member's term (adopted June 21, 1976). B-3001 provides that the first applicant receiving four votes is appointed and vacancies filled within thirty (30) days (adopted March 17, 1998; revised September 2003). B-4001 requires unedited cablecast except where comments violate Regulation 9130, the Open Meetings Act or FERPA (adopted March 17, 1998).

2015_076_022415mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education special meeting of February 24, 2015, called for 5:30 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Three action items are presented: appointment of Stephanie Maynard as Director of Finance under a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure effective February 25, 2015; authorization to finalize a contract with Lecole Planners to provide owner's representative services for the 2014 bond projects after the resignation of Jasen Witt; and award of interior painting at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools to Signature Specialty Coatings for $84,000.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

**Meeting**
Special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, February 24, 2015, 5:30 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Public Communication (agenda items); Personnel - Administrative Appointment; Business - Contract for Owner's Representative and Bid Award for Painting at Boulan and Larson Middle Schools; Adjournment.

**Personnel: Director of Finance**
Ms. Stephanie Maynard is recommended for appointment as Director of Finance. She joined the Troy School District in October 2013 as Accounting Coordinator and was previously a Finance Specialist with Plante Moran for 6 years and a Cost Accountant with Comerica Bank for 2 1/2 years. She earned a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration in 2004 and a Master of Business Administration with a concentration in accounting and taxation in 2007 (Wayne State University, August 2007). The suggested resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, with duties beginning February 25, 2015. Her resume lists 18327 Winterset Drive, Southfield, MI 48076, (248) 469-5246, StephanieKMaynard@gmail.com, and roles at Plante Moran as Governmental Accounting Professional (September 2010 - October 2013) and Senior Auditor (August 2007 - September 2010), and at Comerica Bank, Detroit, as Cost Accountant (November 2004 - March 2007).

**Business: Owner's Representative**
The resignation of Jasen Witt left a vacancy in the owner's representative role, described as essential to bond project management as a direct liaison between the District and its construction manager, architect and contractors. The resolution authorizes administration to finalize the contract with Lecole Planners; the representative will manage architects, engineers, construction managers and contractors, ensure projects are on schedule and within approved budgets, and approve change orders of amounts deemed appropriate by administration. A February 12, 2015 memorandum from Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, to Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky states that after discussions with Machesky and Rob Carson he recommends Lecole Planners, a one-person business owned and operated by Michelle Kerns, an architect by trade whom West worked with during his time in Royal Oak. Dana Abrahams of Clark Hill was asked to draft the contract for approval at the February 24, 2015 meeting.

Michelle Kerns, AIA, CFD, 43450 Reservoir, Plymouth, MI 48170, (248) 921-3929, has run Lecole Planners LLC since 2001. Selected experience:

| Client | Period | Scale |
|---|---|---|
| Huron Valley Schools | 2001 - present (bond 2001-2007) | $103.9 million bond program; sinking fund $2.0 million annually |
| Royal Oak School District | December 2007 - present | Sinking fund $2.1 million annually |
| Northville Public Schools | January 2012 - present | Sinking fund $2.2 million annually |
| Baker College, Allen Park | March 2014 - present | Facility assessment and visioning |
| Trenton Public Schools | December 2008 - August 2011 | 2008 bond issue |
| Woodhaven Brownstown | November 2004 - December 2007 | 2002 bond issue |

She was an architect and project manager at URS Corporation from 1990 to 2001 and an intern architect at Neumann/Smith and Associates from 1985 to 1990, and holds a BS in Architecture from the University of Michigan (1991, Magna Cum Laude).

**Business: Painting Bid**
Bids for interior painting at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools were reviewed by Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor, and Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations. The resolution awards the bid to Signature Specialty Coatings in the amount of $84,000.00 as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Carson's February 18, 2015 memorandum on Public Bid 9800 states the scope is wall preparation and painting of hallways, restrooms, cafeteria, gymnasium and locker rooms under the District Deferred Maintenance Painting Schedule, and that Signature Specialty Coatings is the low qualified bidder.

PERSONNEL - ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, DIRECTOR OF FINANCE. The superintendent recommends the appointment of Ms. Stephanie Maynard to the position of Director of Finance. Ms. Maynard came to the Troy School District in October of 2013 as the Accounting Coordinator. Prior to Troy she was a Finance Specialist with Plante Moran for 6 years and a Cost Accountant with Comerica Bank for 2 1/2 years. She received a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration in 2004 and a Master's degree in Business Administration with a concentration in accounting and taxation in 2007. The suggested resolution states that the Board of Education issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Stephanie Maynard, who will begin her duties as Director of Finance effective February 25, 2015, with blanks for the mover, supporter, and yes and no votes.

The attached resume identifies Stephanie K. Maynard, 18327 Winterset Drive, Southfield, MI 48076, (248) 469-5246, StephanieKMaynard@gmail.com, citing more than ten years of general accounting experience and more than six years of public accounting experience. As Accounting Coordinator at the Troy School District from October 2013 to the present, in a supervisory role, she supervises and evaluates business office staff covering payroll, accounts payable and general ledger accounting; prepares financial reports for federal, state and local grant reporting agencies; prepares the schedule of financial assistance for federally funded programs, audit work papers, and Consolidated Annual Financial Reports; prepares monthly bank reconciliations, monthly financial reports for Board review, and monthly budget to actual analysis reports for the Assistant Superintendent of Business Services and/or Superintendent; maintains the District's chart of accounts, the record of all financial transactions and investment and interest records; tracks, processes and records District debt service; reviews and approves all journal entries; and supports the District's accounting software with emphasis on internal controls and system security. At Plante Moran in Southfield, Michigan she was a Governmental Accounting Professional from September 2010 to October 2013, providing temporary financial management for school districts, year-end audit preparation, federal and local financial reports, emergency assistance rebuilding accounting history, monthly bank reconciliations, board presentations to those charged with governance, and preparation of budget amendments and cash flow projections. She was a Senior Auditor at Plante Moran from August 2007 to September 2010, conducting financial and compliance engagements, supervising junior auditors, and developing audit programs and testing procedures. She was a Cost Accountant at Comerica Bank in Detroit from November 2004 to March 2007, creating controls for data accumulation and reporting systems, reporting on periodic variances, applying overhead costs under generally accepted accounting principles, and assisting the Controller with quarterly financial reports. Her education is a Master of Business Administration with a concentration in accounting and taxation from Wayne State University, Detroit, Michigan, August 2007.

BUSINESS - APPOINTMENT OF OWNER'S REPRESENTATIVE. With the resignation of Jasen Witt, a vacancy was left in the owner's representative role he served; the packet describes the role as essential to bond project management because it provides the expertise of a direct liaison between the District and its construction manager, architect and contractors. The suggested resolution recites that it is the desire of the Board of Education to hire an owner's representative to oversee the capital projects associated with the 2014 bond issue, that the owner's representative will have the responsibility of managing the architects, engineers, construction managers and contractors, ensuring projects are on schedule and within approved budgets, and approving change orders of amounts deemed appropriate by administration, and resolves that the Troy Board of Education authorize administration to proceed with finalizing the contract with Lecole Planners to provide owner representative services.

A memorandum dated February 12, 2015 from Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services (Business Office, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013) to Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, states that after discussions with the superintendent and with Rob Carson he recommends proceeding with the hiring of Lecole Planners to serve as owner's representative for the bond projects. Lecole Planners is a one-person business owned and operated by Michelle Kerns, an architect by trade with many years of experience in the owner's representative role. West notes he worked with Michelle during his time in Royal Oak, where she was instrumental in ensuring projects were on schedule and within budget, and that her attention to detail and ability to work with the construction manager, architect and contractors brings a value that will pay for her services. He states he asked Dana Abrahams of Clark Hill to draft a contract for owner's representative with the goal of having a recommendation approved by the board at the February 24, 2015 Board of Education meeting.

The attached resume identifies Michelle Kerns, AIA, CFD, Educational Planner and Consultant, 43450 Reservoir, Plymouth MI 48170, (248) 921-3929. She has owned Lecole Planners LLC since 2001. For Huron Valley Schools (2001 to present) she served as owner's representative for a $103.9 million dollar bond program covering 2001 to 2007 and assists with the Building Site Sinking Fund Program, an annual program of $2.0 million; duties included monitoring budgets, reviewing drawings, contract negotiations, construction administration, change order evaluation, and liaison among school buildings, administration, the construction manager and architect. For Royal Oak School District (December 2007 to present) she served as owner's representative for the final phase of a three-phase bond construction project and since 2012 oversees Building Site Sinking Fund projects, an annual program of $2.1 million, acting as liaison to the City Engineer, preparing punchlists, reviewing billings and assisting with submissions to the State of Michigan. For Northville Public Schools (January 2012 to present) she oversees select Building Site Sinking Fund projects, an annual program of $2.2 million, and conducted a district-wide facility assessment used for multi-year master planning. For Baker College, Allen Park Campus (March 2014 to present) she works with the college president on a facility assessment and visioning exercise. For Trenton Public Schools (December 2008 to August 2011) she consulted on the 2008 Bond Issue, and for Woodhaven Brownstown School District (November 2004 to December 2007) on the 2002 Bond Issue, including coordinating replacement of 75% of all furniture.

At URS Corporation from 1990 to 2001 she was an architect and project manager. As Project Principal for Farmington Public Schools she prepared a bond issue application including more than 100 million dollars of proposed construction in 25 buildings and served as project manager overseeing work at 25 school facilities in 4 years. As Project Manager at the Wayne R.E.S.A. Educational Center in Wayne, Michigan she managed 10 separate renovation projects over a 6 year period with an aggregate construction cost of 2.4 million and redesigned the main auditorium for television production and teleconferencing. As Project Manager for Huron Valley Schools in Highland, Michigan she served over a 10 year period implementing projects under 2 separate bond issues and a sinking fund. She was Project Architect for Lake Orion Community Schools remodeling four elementary schools. For South Redford Public Schools her bond planning determined a facility improvement program of 33 million against needs in excess of 80 million, and for Lincoln Consolidated School District in Ypsilanti a total bond issue amount of 43 million that led to a new middle school, absorption of the existing middle school into the high school, remodeling of all elementary schools and a new bus facility. She was an intern architect at Neumann/Smith and Associates from 1985 to 1990. Education: BS / 1991 / Architecture / University of Michigan, graduated Magna Cum Laude; registered architect State of Wisconsin; AIA National and Detroit Chapters; MSBO Certified Facility Director. References: Ms. Jackie Johnston, Superintendent, L'Anse Creuse Public Schools (586) 783-6300; Dr. Nancy Coratti, Deputy Superintendent, Huron Valley Schools (248) 684-8000; Mr. Mike Zopf, Assistant Superintendent, Northville Public Schools (248) 344-8444; Ms. Kris Barann, President, Baker College (313) 425-3727, formerly with Trenton Public Schools; Dr. Robert Maxfield, Professor, Oakland University (248) 370-3087, formerly with Farmington Public Schools; and Mr. Paul Gmelin, Principal, Lakeland High School, Huron Valley Schools (248) 676-8323.

BUSINESS - PAINTING AT BOULAN AND LARSON MIDDLE SCHOOLS. Bid responses for interior painting at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools were reviewed by Mr. Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor, and Mr. Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations. The suggested resolution provides that the bid for interior painting at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools be awarded to Signature Specialty Coatings in the amount of $84,000.00 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. A memorandum dated February 18, 2015 from Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance & Operations (Operations Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, phone 248.823.4050, fax 248.823.4077) to Superintendent Rich Machesky, concerning Contracted Painting Bid - Public Bid 9800, states that an RFP was created to obtain competitive bids for interior painting at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools, with a scope of work providing wall preparation and painting to the hallways, restrooms, cafeteria, gymnasium and locker rooms, as part of the District Deferred Maintenance Painting Schedule. The memo states that Signature Specialty Coatings is the low qualified bidder, that the total project cost requested for award is $84,000.00, and that funding for the purchase will be from the Capital Projects Fund. Copies were sent to Pat Orczykowski of the Business Department and to the Purchasing Department file.
